title: Letter 14 — No Repentance Too Late
attribution_note: Letter 14 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: Why I did not receive you

pairs.en: You wished to come to me — but in what spirit, I do not know. God knows your heart. I did not receive you, and not without cause.

When a man has once been deceived by someone, he does not trust him again. And so the lying and the deceitful uproot all trust from human hearts, until we often do not believe even good people. It is pitiful that such tares are to be found among Christians. God sees them, and men are already beginning to discern them. God sees them, and bears with them *“until the harvest.”* Then shall they be gathered into their own bundles, and delivered to the eternal fire *“to burn them.”* [Matthew 13:30]
I forgive you everything that you have done to me, and I wish for you all that I wish for myself. Therefore, for my sake, be at peace and of a quiet mind — only do not forsake yourself.

Understand what I write. Whatever a man does in this world, God sees it all, and writes it down in His book. All that is of the world will remain in the world; but a man's deeds alone will go with him to the world to come, and the more good or evil deeds he does here, the more of them will appear there. *“Whatsoever a man soweth,”* here, *“that shall he also reap”* there [Galatians 6:7]. Every man's labour and its fruit will appear there: with the good, good will appear; with the evil, evil. Woe to the wretched man in that hour, when all his evil deeds — which he wrought from his youth even to his end — are laid bare before the righteous Judge and before the whole world, and it is said of him: “Behold the man, and his deeds!” Of this God Himself now speaks to the sinner: *“I will rebuke thee, and set thy sins in order before thine eyes”* [Psalm 49:21].

The more a man twists the rope, the longer it grows; and the more he lays upon himself, the heavier the burden becomes; and the more he tangles himself in the net, the harder it is to free himself from it; and the more he blackens himself, the harder it is to wash himself clean. Do you understand what I write?...

Enough of twisting the rope — it is time to break it off; enough of burdening yourself — it is time to throw off the burden; enough of tangling yourself in the net — it is time to tear the net asunder and be free; enough of blackening yourself still more — it is time to be washed clean. God is a Helper in everything. Only rise, and God will lift you up; begin, and God will help you; take heart, and God will strengthen you; awake, and Christ will enlighten you; set your foot upon the path of the godly, and Christ will lead you.

*“Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light”* [Ephesians 5:14]. It is time, it is time — O, it is time! *“It is time for thee, LORD, to work”* [Psalm 118:126].

A man does not know where the judgment of God will overtake him, and there he will fall into the pit where he least looks for it. Pharaoh, king of Egypt, pursued after Israel, and sought to lead the people of God back into captivity; and where he thought to win himself profit and spoil, there he won himself a grave. This enemy of God is set forth as an example to all the world. And there are many Pharaohs even now. But I wish upon no one what befell Pharaoh; rather I wish for all what the prodigal son did. Then there will be *“joy in the presence of the angels of God,”* according to the word of the Lord [Luke 15:10].

sections.heading: Not the beginning, but the end

pairs.en: There is no repentance that is too late, so long as a man lives in this world. Only of that repentance which comes upon a sick man at the very point of death — a man who has lived all his former days in sins, without repentance — I say nothing: with what hope such a one departs from this world, God alone knows. Therefore it is better to repent beforehand, and to begin a new Christian life; then a man will depart with good hope.

It is not the beginning, but the end, that is praised. Begin while you are still in health; and even if death soon overtakes you, you will be saved, and none of your sins will be remembered before God. So mighty is true repentance before God — but repentance joined with faith in Christ! Read, moreover, Romans 2:3, and what follows.
